basis: Total ophthalmoplegia, ptosis and iris abnormalities define an ocular disorder; no established extraocular neurologic disease.
Zellweger-spectrum disease has defining metabolic, brain and liver abnormalities; hearing loss affects most; retinal disease omitted because of cap.
Primary microcephaly and intellectual disability occur in 8/8 patients; speech delay is also neurologic.
Hereditary cerebellar degeneration with neurologic manifestations across the included subtypes.
V-ATPase-related glycosylation disease characteristically causes cutis laxa; neurodevelopmental impairment affects most in the classical phenotype.
Cerebellar ataxia and sensory neuropathy affect the central and peripheral nervous systems; impaired pursuit does not establish ocular disease.
Autoimmune CNS disease defined by refractory seizures and progressive cognitive dysfunction.
Hypomyelination and neurodevelopmental degeneration define disease; skeletal muscle atrophy documented in 4/4 patients supports muscle involvement.
Astrocytic tumor arising in the central nervous system.
Defining heart-hand syndrome combines digital and joint malformations with cardiac conduction defects.
Autoimmune thyroid disease defines syndrome; gastritis/celiac disease and macrocytic anemia each occur in 30-79% as components of the syndrome.
Radio-digital dysplasia identifies skeletal malformations; supplied information does not establish other functional organ involvement.
Hereditary Wilms tumor is a renal nephroblastoma.
Tumor originates in the uterine corpus, a reproductive organ outside the axes; germ-cell histology does not establish endocrine disease.
Combined T/B-cell immunodeficiency; Kaposi sarcoma remains a separately diagnosed malignancy despite occurring in 3/3 reported patients.
Neurodevelopmental abnormalities and thoracic hypoplasia define syndrome; low IgA alone does not establish functional immunodeficiency; pigment spots are non-damaging.
Hypogonadism and developmental disability predominate; skeletal and structural dental defects each 30-79%; ocular findings omitted by cap; asthma/otitis are separate diseases.
Localized adenocarcinoma occupies lung epithelium without stromal, vascular or pleural invasion.
Benign ovarian teratoma; thyroid-type tissue is histology rather than thyroid gland disease. Functional hyperthyroidism occurs in a small minority.
Umbrella disease of multiple endocrine glands; autoimmunity and extraendocrine injury are not established across the group.
Defining preaxial polydactyly affects the skeleton and upper-back hypertrichosis affects hair.
Systemic Streptobacillus infection; inflammatory polyarthritis occurs in approximately 50%; transient rash does not establish skin damage.
Microcephaly and developmental disability predominate; brachydactyly and clinodactyly occur in 30-79%; dysplastic pinnae alone do not establish hearing damage.
Mesenchymal soft-tissue sarcoma typically involving deep proximal pelvic and perineal tissues; genital location does not imply endocrine disease.
Intestinal hookworms attach to and injure bowel mucosa; iron-deficiency anemia depends on infection burden and is a separate diagnosis; skin/lung phases are transient.
